MRI of left Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, AX T2W FS, CO T2W FS, SG T1W



> Fracture of posterior aspect of tibial intercondylar eminence of left proximal tibia with displaced bony fragment, just at PCL attchment, C/W avulsion fracture of PCL. 
> Bone marrow edema over left proximal tibia and lower pole of patella.
> The contour of PCL not all in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside on F/S T2WI, in favor of partial tear.
  Interstitial increase signal intensity of ACL on F/S T2WI, infavor of grade 1 injury.
> Lipohemarthrosis of left knee and suprapatellar bursitis; mild deep infrapatellar bursitis.
> Generalized soft tissue swelling over left knee, including subcutaneous and muscular layer and increased fat stranding over intermuscular region.
> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, in favor of grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to degeneration or contusion.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Mild interstitial increased signal intensity of quadriceps tendon and distal patellar tendon on F/S T2WI, in favor of tendinosis or grade 1 injury.
> Increased fat stranding and minimal fluid accumulation located along the pes anserinus, reflecting Anserine bursitis

Impression: 
1. C/W PCL avulsion fracture and partial tear of PCL.
2. Grade 1 injury of ACL.
3. Left tibial intercondylar eminence fracture with bone marrow edema over left proximal tibia; bone contusion of left lower patella.
4. Lipohemarthrosis of left knee.
5. Subcutaneous and muscle edema around left knee and intermuscular edema.
6. Anserine bursitis.
7. Grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to degeneration or contusion.
8. Tendinosis or grade 1 injury of patellar tendon and quadriceps tendon.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and further management

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed..

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

The medial collateral ligament, posterior oblique ligament, fibular collateral ligament, popliteus and biceps femoris tendon attachments, as well as iliotibial band are intact.

Mild quadriceps and patellar tendinosis without tears. The patellar retinacula are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 6 mm, within normal limits.

Preserved patellofemoral articular cartilage. Preserved medial and lateral femorotibial articular cartilage.

Trace knee joint fluid. Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration. Bone islands in the distal femur and proximal tibia.

1. Inferiorly surfacing incomplete tear or of the medial meniscus extending into the body, with medial meniscal extrusion and adjacent parameniscal cyst formation.
2. Quadriceps and patellar tendinosis without tears.

Imagen altamente sugerente de infarto óseo de la región diafisaria distal del fémur.

Няма данни за ставен излив. Нормално изобразяване на латералния менискус. Предна и задна кръстна връзка – б.о. Колатерални лигаменти – б.о. Ретинакулуми – б.о. Патела, хрущял на пателата – б.о. Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Bucket-handle tear medial meniscus of left knee as current injury
Comparison: 1/[DATE]

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla. system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
There is moderate subcortical cystic change in the patella likely related to overlying chondromalacia. The Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal. Previously identified linear hyperintense focus is no longer seen.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: There is severe chondromalacia patella most pronounced at the apex and inferior aspect of the lateral facet..

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. 

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
Again noted is tendinosis at the origin of the medial head of the gastrocnemius. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.


IMPRESSION:
1. Severe chondromalacia patella.
2. No meniscal tear identified. 
3. Tendinosis at the origin of the medial head of the gastrocnemius, left pronounced than on the prior study.

original_report:
Antecedentes Clínicos:
Lesiones degenerativas mediales.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones difusas de señal de la médula ósea.
Adelgazamiento condral difuso de espesor total de la región anterior y central de carga del
compartimento femorotibial medial. Esto se asocia a moderado edema óseo regional de ambas
superficies, con esclerosis subcondral y osteofitos marginales.
Ligamentos conservados y colaterales de grosor y señal conservados.
El menisco lateral presenta fibrilación difusa de su borde libre, con alteración de señal
intrasustancia del cuerno anterior de carácter degenerativo.
Moderada extrusión del menisco medial, con rotura radial de los dos tercios internos del cuerno
posterior. Rotura compleja de la región corporal, con fibrilación del borde libre, un componente
vertical oblicuo y otro horizontal, que determina desplazamiento de tejido meniscal al receso
menisco tibial. Moderado edema parameniscal.
Irregularidad superficial difusa del cartílago del compartimento femorotibial lateral.
Moderado adelgazamiento condral con úlceras de espesor total en la región central y faceta
medial de la patela. Irregularidad superficial difusa del cartílago troclear, con adelgazamiento de
espesor moderado en la vertiente medial.
Leve a moderado derrame articular, con leve engrosamiento sinovial difuso. No hay quistes
poplíteos.
Engrosamiento y aumento de señal de la plica patelar medial, que se extiende sobre la vertiente
medial de la tróclea.
Leve engrosamiento y aumento de señal del tendón proximal del gastrocnemio medial, con
imagen sugerente de fina rotura parcial intrasustancia.
Tendones del cuádriceps, patelar, poplíteo, semimembranoso, bíceps femoral, banda iliotibial y
tendones de la pata de ganso de grosor y señal conservado.
Grupos musculares de trofismo y señal conservado.
Impresión:
Rotura radial prácticamente completa del cuerno posterior del menisco medial, con moderada
extrusión meniscal, asociado a una rotura compleja de la región corporal y desplazamiento de
tejido meniscal al receso menisco tibial.
Cambios degenerativos del menisco lateral, con fibrilación difusa del borde libre.
Condropatía femorotibial medial difusa grado 4, con edema óseo regional sugerente de
fenómenos de sobrecarga.
Condropatía femorotibial lateral grado 2. Condropatía patelar grado 3-4 y troclear grado 2-3. Leve a moderado derrame articular, con leve sinovitis difusa.
Engrosamiento y aumento de señal de la plica patelar medial.
Leve tendinosis proximal del gastrocnemio medial, con pequeña rotura parcial intrasustancia.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Anterior knee pain after fall approximately one month prior. Assess for occult stress fracture or meniscus tear.
Comparison: [REDACTED].

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.16 Tesla open system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
No fracture. No suspicious marrow signal abnormality.

JOINT SPACE:
Alignment is anatomic. No joint effusion. No intra-articular body. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Increased signal throughout much of the body and posterior horn compatible with diffuse myxoid degeneration. There is a small oblique undersurface tear at the posterior horn near the posterior root with borderline extrusion of the body. No displaced fragment or para meniscal cyst is identified.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Increased signal at the posterior root attachment not meeting MR chart here for tear, likely representing intrasubstance degeneration. There is borderline extrusion of the body. No displaced fragment or para meniscal cyst is identified.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Mild chondral thinning noted along the weightbearing surface of the lateral femoral condyle near the intercondylar notch.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Small, scattered foci of partial-thickness cartilage loss diffusely noted along the patella. No discrete trochlear defect.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 7 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1. Medial meniscus tear as described. Lateral meniscus degeneration without definite tear.

2. Low-grade patellofemoral/lateral compartment chondrosis.

MRI RIGHT KNEE:

INDICATION:    Patient reports history of chondroblastoma to the right knee diagnosed in <[YEAR]> but not fully worked up. X-ray in <[Month]> <[YEAR]> confirms nonspecific lytic lesion right patella. Please assess.

PRIOR IMAGING: Plain film radiographs from [Date]
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

In the superolateral aspect of the patella there is a T2 bright focus with irregular sclerotic margination seen on the plain film characterized by low signal margination on MRI. This focal lesion has central T2 bright signal similar in signal to articular cartilage and has a linear cartilaginous signal extending posteriorly to the articular surface of patella. The articular cartilage of patella directly posterior to this focus is intact but does demonstrate slight contour irregularity and signal change which may represent mild chondrosis. The finding measures about 1 cm in maximum diameter. The appearance is typical in location and MRI features of a dorsal defect of the patella. This represents a normal anatomic variant.

Articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint is well-maintained.

The extensor mechanism is intact.

The patellofemoral ligaments are intact and appear unremarkable. The TT-TG distance measures about 1.5 cm, at the upper limits of normal, consistent with an element of mild lateralization of the tibial tubercle

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

Within the lateral femoral condyle there is a serpiginously marginated lesion measuring 2.1 AP, 1.4 cm with an 0.9 cm in depth situated 2 to 3 mm deep to the cortex of the lateral femoral condyle. The rim of this lesion is T2 bright and T1 dark with central fat. MR features are typical of a bone infarct. No evidence of cortical collapse.

The medial meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is well-maintained.

The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex including the IT band, fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is a trace Baker's cyst demonstrated. No significant knee effusion is demonstrated.

A few small subcentimeter popliteal lymph nodes are incidentally noted.

Marrow signal is otherwise normal. No other bone infarcts are seen within field-of-view.

INTERPRETATION: 
Subcortical chondroid focus in the superolateral aspect of patella has MR features typical of a dorsal defect of the patella. The finding is not typical of a chondroblastoma. Mild overlying chondromalacia patella.

Mild lateralization of tibial tubercle.

Trace Baker's cyst.

There is a bone infarct seen in the lateral femoral condyle. No evidence of articular collapse.
Clinical correlation as to the possible cause of a bone infarct in this patient is recommended.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: pain
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Lobular T2 hyperintense lesion in the right medial distal femoral metaphysis measuring 1.7 x 1.6 x 2.3 cm with with stippled hyperintense signal, compatible with a low-grade chondroid lesion. Background marrow signal is otherwise normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Trace joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Mild myxoid degeneration of the medial meniscus without discrete tear.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: High-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss along the posterior lateral tibial plateau. Minimal heterogeneity along the central weightbearing lateral femoral condyle.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Diffuse high-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss along the articular surface with focal full-thickness chondral fissuring along the inferior lateral trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: Mild edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. Lateral patellar tilt and translation. Patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Top normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 17 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Findings of lateral patellofemoral maltracking with impingement of Hoffa's fat pad and high-grade patellofemoral chondrosis.
2.	Additional moderate lateral compartment chondrosis.
3.	Low-grade chondroid lesion in the right medial distal femoral metaphysis, for which follow-up MRI is recommended in 6-12 months.

COMMUNICATION FOLLOW-UP: [REDACTED]. [REDACTED]

3. Degeneration of meniscus and tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus and anterior horn of lateral meniscus.
4. Mild synovitis of left and and patellar plicae.

Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]

MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla extremity system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small partially ruptured Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Full-thickness cartilage fissuring medial patellar facet and median ridge with subchondral bone marrow edema. Partial-thickness cartilage loss lateral patellar facet. Full-thickness cartilage fissuring central trochlea with subchondral cystic change and intense subchondral bone marrow edema.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: There is edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. There is lateral patellar tilt and translation. No patella alta. Shallow trochlea and elongated lateral patellar facet. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 10 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Findings of active lateral patellar maltracking with high grade patellofemoral chondrosis.

Zentrierte Stellung der Gelenkpartner im rechten Kniegelenk. Patella zentriert ohne Hoch- oder Tiefstand. Degenerative Veränderungen betont im medialen femorotibialen Gelenk mit Gelenkspaltverschmälerung und osteophytären Ausziehungen femoral und am Tibiaplateau (5/19). Subchondrales Ödem an der medialen Femurkondyle angrenzend (5/18). Deutliche Ausdünnung des Knorpelbesatz des im medialen Kompartiment mit perifokal vollschichtige Chondropathie angrenzend an das Ödemsignal. Retropatellar fokal bis vollschichtige Chondropathie medialseitig (4/14). Fokal oberflächliche Chondropathie im lateralen femorotibialen Kompartiment (5/20). Gering steifige Signalanhebungen im Außenmeniskusvorderhorn und - hinterhorn. Komplexe Rissbildung am Innenmeniskushinterhorn mit Ausläufern bis an die tibiale Insertion (5/23+ 24, 6/13). Innenmeniskusvorderhorn mit geringen Signalanhebungen ohne Rissbildung.

МР находка: Костите, формиращи лявата колянна става, са с нормална форма и сигнален интензитет. Наличие на минимален ставен излив. Артикулиращият хрущял на фемура и тибията е със запазена дебелина и конгруентност.
МР данни за лезия в задния рог на латералния менискус. В него се изобразяява хиперинтензна линия с хоризонтален ход, съответстваща на скъсване. Руптурата достига до края на менискуса и се проследява в тялото му и частично в предния му рог. Предният рог на латералния менискус е с дифузно повишен сигнал. Целият латерален менискус е експулсиран встрани. Между него и латералния колатерален лигамент са налице едемни промени в мастната тъкан. МР данни за частична увреда в задния рог на медиалния менискус. В него се вижда хиперинтензна линия с кос ход, не достигаща до артикулиращите повърхности на тибията и фемура. Нормален МР образ на предния рог на медиалния менискус.
Кръстни връзки – със запазена цялост. Вижда се частична увреда на латералния колатерален лигамент. Същият е задебелен и с дифузно повишен сигнален интензитет на инсерцията си за фемура, като измененията са на протежение от около 10-11мм. Медиален колатерален лигамент – б.о. Лигамент на пателата, сухожилие на м. квадрицепс феморис – без особености. Нормално изобразяване на пателата. Вижда се малък дефект от медиалната страна на хрущяла на пателата. Дефектът не достига до костта и е с размери 2,5/2,0 мм. Ретинакулуми на пателата – със запазена цялост. Поплитеална ямка – наличие на мултилокуларна Бекерова киста с типично местоположение и размери 44/37/16 мм. Мускулни групи, останали меки тъкани – нормално изобразяване. Заключение:  МР данни за хоризонтална руптура в задния рог на латералния менискус - grade 3. Дегенеративни промени в предния рог на латералния менискус. Частична увреда на задния рог на медиалния меднискус – grade 2a. Увреда на латералния колатерален лигамент – grade 1.  Минимален ставен излив. Хондромалация на пателата – grade 3. Мултилокуларна Бекерова киста с типично местоположение.

MRI of left Knee with 
-3-Plane Loc LT, Sag PD FS, Sag T2 FS, Ax T2 FS, Ax DWI B800, Screen Save, Sag T1, Cor T2 FS, ADC (10^-6 mm?s):[DATE] [TIME]



> Some osteophytes and irregular thining of intra-articular cartilage of left knee, reflecting osteoarthritis
  Wearing of articular cartilage and tiny subchondral cyst over patellar ridge, reflecting grade 3-4 chondromalacia (Srs/Img: [ID].
> Patellar enthesophyte; tendinosis of quadriceps tendon and iliotibial band.
> Mild fat stranding over suprapatellar fat pad, R/O suprapatellar fat pad impingement syndrome
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
  Lobulated hyperintensity foci with internal septums in retrocondylar region of left knee, reflecting retrocondylar bursitis/ gastrocnemius bursitis.
  Small Baker's cyst and popliteus bursitis.
> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, in favor of grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to degeneration or meniscal vascularity. 
> Mild interstitial increased signal intensity of ACL on F/S T2WI, in favor of degeneration.
> PCL, medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Subcutaneous infiltration over left anterior knee.

Impression: 
1. Osteoarthritis of left knee, more prominent at patellofemoral joint with focal grade 3-4 chondromalacia. 
2. Mild synovitis of left knee with patellar plicae and small Baker's cyst and retrocondylar bursitis/ gastrocnemius bursitis. (Srs/Img: [ID]; 6/9-14)
4. Grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to degeneration or meniscal vascularity.
5. Mild subcutaneous edema over left anterior knee.
6. Suprapatellar fat pad impingement syndrome and tendinosis of quadriceps tendon.
7. Degeneration of ACL.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and physical examination

Right knee MRI without contrast:

INDICATION: Rule out right knee meniscal tear.

COMPARISON: No prior for comparison.

FINDINGS:

No significant effusion. No loose body.

Anterior compartment:
Overall mildly chondrosis with small fissures on the lateral and medial facets of the patella less than 50% of the thickness. Area of subchondral sclerosis on the lateral facet. Patellar and quadriceps tendons intact. Retinacula are intact. Hoffa fat pad unremarkable.

Medial compartment:
Mild chondrosis. Presence of a small meniscal flounce in the anterior body of medial meniscus without definitive tear. Capsular meniscal interface intact. Medial collateral ligament intact. Pes anserine unremarkable. Moderate insertional tendinopathy within the semimembranosus tendon.

Lateral compartment:
Mild chondrosis no significant meniscal tear. Lateral collateral ligament intact. Biceps femoris tendon intact. Iliotibial band intact. Popliteus tendon is intact.

Intercondylar compartment:
Mild cystic changes within the tibial eminence and mild high signal intensity within the anterior cruciate ligament and could be in keeping with intraligamentous beginning degenerative mucoid changes. Posterior cruciate ligament intact.

Multiple varicose veins on the medial aspect of the knee in the subcutaneous tissues.

CONCLUSION:
1. Mild to moderate patellofemoral chondrosis.
2. Semimembranosus insertional tendinosis without tear. No discrete ligament or meniscal tear identified.
3. Multiple varicose veins to the medial aspect of the knee in the subcutaneous tissue.

MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION:    [Age] male complaining of left knee pain and swelling. Ultrasound shows focal tear of the lateral collateral ligament versus ligament sprain and likely tear of the medial and lateral meniscus. Joint effusion in the suprapatellar recess and Baker's cyst. Recommended by radiologist.

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

There is mild thickening and increased T2 signal in the proximal fibers of the patellar tendon. Findings are consistent with mild patellar tendinosis. Quadriceps and patellofemoral ligaments are intact and appear unremarkable.

The articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint demonstrates mild chondral fraying at the patellar apex and also within the femoral trochlea but overall cartilage is reasonably well-maintained. The TT-TG distance is within normal limits.

There is mild non-surfacing signal seen in the posterior horn of medial meniscus peripherally. Involving posterior horn near the posterior root attachment of medial meniscus there is mild apical truncation and fraying of the meniscus consistent with a subtle radial tear. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment demonstrates regions of chondral fraying and thinning with a few subcortical cysts seen within the weightbearing surface of the medial femoral condyle in keeping with moderate chondrosis.

There is a subtle tear in the lateral meniscus involving anterior horn and anterior body in keeping with the radial tear in this region. There is also a horizontal signal in keeping with a horizontal tear extending into the anterior horn of lateral meniscus. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment demonstrates chondral fraying and thinning but is reasonably well-maintained. Findings are consistent with moderate chondrosis. Minimal degenerative spurring to the lateral joint compartment is noted.

The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex including the IT band, the fibular collateral ligament, the biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is a small Baker's cyst. There is edema and fluid seen around the pes anserine tendons consistent with pes anserine bursitis.

There is a small knee effusion. Mild reactive synovitis is noted.

Marrow signal is within normal limits.

INTERPRETATION: 

Mild tricompartmental chondrosis with early degenerative spurring to the lateral joint margin.

Subtle meniscal tears to the lateral and medial menisci as described.

Small Baker's cyst.

Pes anserine bursitis.

MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. Mild marrow edema along the peripheral aspect of the lateral femoral condyle, likely represents contusion from a recent lateral patellar dislocation. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Cartilage heterogeneity along the median patellar ridge and lateral patellar facet.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Low grade 2 sprain of the MPFL and medial patellar retinacula.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Findings of patellofemoral maltracking with osseous contusion along the lateral femoral condyle suggesting a recent lateral patellar dislocation, as described above.
2.	Low grade 2 sprain of the MPFL and medial patellar retinacula.
3.	Moderate knee joint effusion.
4.	Low-grade patellofemoral compartment chondrosis.
